The primary study is **“p8 Deficiency causes siderosis in spleens and lymphocyte apoptosis in acute pancreatitis”** (2014; **PMID 25098696**). Compared with matched wild-type mice, mature p8/Nupr1−/− mice had splenic siderosis. During experimental acute pancreatitis, knockout mice showed greater lymphocyte declines and significantly increased splenic apoptosis. Ceruletide (cerulein) is listed in the paper’s MeSH terms; the abstract does not specify the induction protocol or dose.

Yes—in a mouse study, **p8/NUPR1-deficient mice had splenic siderosis**, and during experimentally induced acute pancreatitis they showed **increased splenic apoptosis and greater loss of CD3+ and CD3+CD4+ lymphocytes** compared with wild-type mice. The siderosis was reported in mature knockout mice; the increased lymphocyte apoptosis was observed during pancreatitis. This is preclinical evidence, not proof of the same effect in humans.
